title: An Empirical Model of Large-Batch Training
one_line: The gradient noise scale predicts the largest useful batch size across many tasks, and that batch size rises as training loss falls.

title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
one_line: Training loss follows power laws in parameters, data and compute, and in training steps at a fixed model.

title: On Layer Normalization in the Transformer Architecture
one_line: Shows Post-LN transformers need learning-rate warm-up because their output-side gradients are unstable at initialization, while Pre-LN trains without warm-up at comparable quality.
formula: Pre-LN: x_{l+1} = x_l + F(LN(x_l)); Post-LN: x_{l+1} = LN(x_l + F(x_l))

title: Lookup-Table Recurrent Language Models for Long Tail Speech Recognition
one_line: An extra embedding table for the previous N-gram scales an RNN language model at constant compute.

title: Wide Neural Networks Forget Less Catastrophically
one_line: Shows that wider networks forget earlier tasks less when trained on new ones; the study varies width, not depth.

title: Deduplicating Training Data Mitigates Privacy Risks in Language Models
one_line: Shows that duplicated sequences in web-scraped corpora drive most successful extraction attacks, and that a sequence seen ten times is regenerated far more often than one seen once.
formula: regeneration frequency grows superlinearly with training-set repeat count (about 1000x for 10 repeats vs 1)

title: Quantifying Memorization Across Neural Language Models
one_line: Reports that verbatim memorization of training text grows with model size, with how often a sequence is duplicated, and with the amount of prompt context, in roughly log-linear form.
formula: log-linear relationships in model size, duplicate count and prompt context (no explicit equation read from abstract)

title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
one_line: Fits a compute-optimal allocation between model size and training tokens, with the power-law form used as the baseline for later schedule-aware laws.

title: Scaling Laws and Interpretability of Learning from Repeated Data
one_line: Shows that a small slice of data repeated many times can seriously degrade a large model even when most of the training data is unique, with the damage tied to memorization of the repeated slice.

title: Memorization Without Overfitting: Analyzing the Training Dynamics of Large Language Models
one_line: Larger models memorize faster and forget less during training across the settings tested, so memorization can rise without overfitting.

title: Measuring Forgetting of Memorized Training Examples
one_line: Trained models forget memorized examples over time, and deterministic training did not forget in their experiments, pointing to nondeterminism as the cause.

title: Large Language Models Struggle to Learn Long-Tail Knowledge
one_line: Finds that a model answers a fact more reliably when the pretraining corpus contains more documents about that fact's entity, so rare facts need many repeats.

title: Scaling Laws for Forgetting When Fine-Tuning Large Language Models
one_line: Measures loss of previously held abilities during fine-tuning, including LoRA, and reports forgetting as a shifted power law in both the number of update steps and the number of fine-tuned parameters.
formula: forgetting ~ shifted power law in update steps and fine-tuned parameter count (exact equation not in abstract)

title: Unraveling the Mystery of Scaling Laws: Part I
one_line: Reports power laws between loss and training step and notes that finite batch sizes make the fit harder.

title: Simple and Scalable Strategies to Continually Pre-train Large Language Models
one_line: Shows that re-warming the learning rate, re-decaying it and replaying a share of old data can match full retraining, and proposes schedules that are not tied to a fixed token budget.

title: Physics of Language Models: Part 3.3, Knowledge Capacity Scaling Laws
one_line: Estimates that a language model stores about 2 bits of knowledge per parameter when trained to sufficiency, and that the number of exposures per fact changes this ratio.
formula: stored knowledge bits ~ 2 x parameter count at sufficient exposure (about 1 bit/param at 100 exposures per fact)

title: MiniCPM: Unveiling the Potential of Small Language Models with Scalable Training Strategies
one_line: Introduces the warmup-stable-decay scheduler, which splits pretraining into warmup, a long constant phase, and a final decay, so training length need not be fixed in advance.

title: Temporal Scaling Law for Large Language Models
one_line: Fits a fixed model's test loss against training steps and predicts later loss from an early window.

title: DeepSeek-V2: A Strong, Economical, and Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Language Model
one_line: Introduces MLA, which caches a small shared latent vector per token instead of full keys and values, mainly to cut inference memory; the page reports model-level results against DeepSeek 67B, not MLA against MHA alone.
formula: c_t = W_DKV h_t; k_t = W_UK c_t; v_t = W_UV c_t; cache only c_t

title: How to set Adam-type optimizer's weight decay as you scale model and dataset size
one_line: Adam-type optimizer weights act as an exponential moving average, so the EMA timescale in epochs (not iterations) is the quantity to hold fixed when scaling, with weight decay falling as dataset size grows.

title: Scaling Laws and Compute-Optimal Training Beyond Fixed Training Durations
one_line: A constant learning rate followed by a short cooldown scales about as predictably as cosine, so one run can be reused across training lengths.

title: Transformers are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality
one_line: Links state-space models and attention through structured matrices and uses that link to build Mamba-2; the fetched page does not compare it against softmax attention at small scale.

title: How Do Large Language Models Acquire Factual Knowledge During Pretraining?
one_line: Facts are learned by slowly raising their probability over steps, with later forgetting eroding part of the gain; forgetting follows a power law in steps, duplicated data forgets faster, and larger batches forget less.

title: Scaling Exponents Across Parameterizations and Optimizers
one_line: Shows many parameterizations, not only muP, support hyperparameter transfer across model size, over tens of thousands of models up to 27B parameters.

title: Scaling Law with Learning Rate Annealing
one_line: Proposes a loss law in the area under the learning-rate curve plus a separate annealing-area term, extending the Chinchilla-style power law to schedules with decay.
formula: L(s) = L0 + A*S1^(-alpha) - C*S2, with S1 the area under the LR curve and S2 the LR annealing area

title: Optimization Hyper-parameter Laws for Large Language Models
one_line: Reports that linear decay gives a slightly lower final loss than cosine at equal token budgets, with the gap larger at smaller budgets.

title: Hyper-Connections
one_line: Widens the residual stream into several learnable streams and beats Pre-Norm at 1B-7B scale.

title: Knowledge Entropy Decay during Language Model Pretraining Hinders New Knowledge Acquisition
one_line: Shows that as pretraining proceeds a model draws on fewer memory sources, which lowers its ability to acquire and retain new knowledge; learning-rate decay is not examined.

title: How Much Can We Forget about Data Contamination?
one_line: Forgetting of early training data is bounded by cumulative Adam-type optimizer weight decay, but measured forgetting is faster than that bound, so the cumulative weight-decay rule under-predicts forgetting.

title: Understanding Warmup-Stable-Decay Learning Rates: A River Valley Loss Landscape Perspective
one_line: Argues that WSD works because pretraining loss has a river-valley shape: the high stable rate makes progress along the valley floor and the fast decay removes oscillation; it does not measure forgetting.

title: Exploring Forgetting in Large Language Model Pre-Training
one_line: Perplexity misses forgetting during pretraining; new entity-memory metrics show forgetting, and light replay reduces it.

title: How Does Critical Batch Size Scale in Pre-training?
one_line: Critical batch size depends mainly on dataset size rather than model size; pretraining runs from 85M to 1.2B parameters on C4 support this, with a muP infinite-width argument.

title: Seq-VCR: Preventing Collapse in Intermediate Transformer Representations for Enhanced Reasoning
one_line: A variance-covariance term on intermediate layers prevents representation collapse and improves arithmetic reasoning.

title: Gated Delta Networks: Improving Mamba2 with Delta Rule
one_line: Combines a data-dependent forget gate with the delta-rule memory update for linear recurrent token mixing; the fetched page names Mamba2 and DeltaNet as baselines and does not confirm a softmax-attention loss comparison.
formula: S_t = S_{t-1} * (alpha_t * (I - beta_t k_t k_t^T)) + beta_t v_t k_t^T; o_t = S_t q_t

title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
one_line: Reuses MLA from DeepSeek-V2 in a larger MoE model; it cites the earlier validation and does not isolate MLA against standard MHA.

title: Peri-LN: Revisiting Normalization Layer in the Transformer Architecture
one_line: Proposes putting a normalization layer on both the input and the output of every sublayer, and argues this gives steadier variance and gradient flow than Pre-LN; the fetched abstract page gives no matched-cell loss numbers.

title: Straight to Zero: Why Linearly Decaying the Learning Rate to Zero Works Best for LLMs
one_line: Finds linear decay all the way to zero slightly beats cosine decay to zero across peak LRs, while cosine to 10 percent of peak beats linear to 10 percent.

title: Muon is Scalable for LLM Training
one_line: Shows Muon scales to a 16B mixture-of-experts model when weight decay and per-parameter update scale are added, with about 2x compute efficiency over an Adam-type optimizer in scaling-law runs.

title: Beyond Cosine Decay: On the effectiveness of Infinite Learning Rate Schedule for Continual Pre-training
one_line: Argues that repeated cosine decay cycles during continual pretraining erase earlier knowledge, and that a schedule without a final decay preserves more of it.

title: A Multi-Power Law for Loss Curve Prediction Across Learning Rate Schedules
one_line: Predicts the whole pretraining loss curve for arbitrary LR schedules from a few runs, and uses the fitted law to search for a schedule that beats cosine.

title: What Matters in Linearizing Language Models? A Comparative Study of Architecture, Scale, and Task Adaptation
one_line: Compares seven subquadratic attention replacements under one controlled distillation setup and finds the gap to softmax appears early and persists through 10B tokens, but this is linearization of pretrained models rather than from-scratch training.

title: Practical Efficiency of Muon for Pretraining
one_line: Pairs Muon with muP and a telescoping search to transfer hyperparameters, and notes that muP estimation error needs multi-scale tuning in practice.

title: Positional Fragility in LLMs: How Offset Effects Reshape Our Understanding of Memorization Risks
one_line: Studies how the position of a sensitive sequence inside the context window changes verbatim memorization; the abstract does not address batch size.

title: Power Lines: Scaling Laws for Weight Decay and Batch Size in LLM Pre-training
one_line: Optimal Adam-type optimizer timescale follows a power law in tokens per parameter, and critical batch size follows a power law in dataset size and is independent of model size.

title: Critical Batch Size Revisited: A Simple Empirical Approach to Large-Batch Language Model Training
one_line: Critical batch size is measured directly with branched training on OLMo 1B and 7B; it starts near zero, rises, then plateaus, and small-run estimates transfer across these sizes.

title: How much do language models memorize?
one_line: Separates memorization from generalization across hundreds of models from 500K to 1.5B parameters and estimates GPT-style capacity at about 3.6 bits per parameter.
formula: capacity ~ 3.6 bits x parameter count; membership inference predicted from capacity versus data size

title: Too Big to Think: Capacity, Memorization, and Generalization in Pre-Trained Transformers
one_line: Finds a trade-off on synthetic tasks: smaller models extrapolate arithmetic but do not memorize facts, while larger models memorize facts but do not extrapolate; capacity is varied via embedding size rather than depth.

title: Latent Multi-Head Attention for Small Language Models
one_line: Trains 30M-parameter GPT models on 100k synthetic stories and finds latent attention with RoPE and half-size latents gives a small validation-loss rise against MHA while cutting KV cache about 45%; without RoPE it does worse than MHA.

title: Beyond Random Sampling: Efficient Language Model Pretraining via Curriculum Learning
one_line: Over 200 models up to 100B tokens show that data ordering, used as a warmup, can speed pretraining.

title: Kimi K2: Open Agentic Intelligence
one_line: Introduces MuonClip, which rescales query and key weights inside Muon to bound attention logits.

title: Fantastic Pretraining Optimizers and Where to Find Them
one_line: Benchmarks pretraining optimizers with per-optimizer tuning and shows that shared hyperparameters bias comparisons.

title: Muon: Training and Trade-offs with Latent Attention and MoE
one_line: Studies Muon on 30M-200M decoders with latent attention and mixture-of-experts layers.

title: What Really Matters in Matrix-Whitening Optimizers?
one_line: SOAP gains the most per step over Muon, and the gap comes mainly from variance adaptation.

title: Kimi Linear: An Expressive, Efficient Attention Architecture
one_line: Kimi Delta Attention adds finer gating to Gated DeltaNet and is reported to beat it and full attention.

title: Hyperparameter Transfer Enables Consistent Gains of Matrix-Preconditioned Optimizers Across Scales
one_line: Derives muP-style scaling for matrix-preconditioned optimizers including Muon, and reports residual finite-width drift that blocking and spectral normalization reduce.

title: Scaling and Transferability of Annealing Strategies in Large Language Model Training
one_line: Studies how the best annealing strategy changes with peak LR, total steps and model size, using an accumulated forward-effect quantity and an annealing-momentum term.

title: Understanding the Mechanisms of Fast Hyperparameter Transfer
one_line: Splits training into a width-stable part that sets the best learning rate and a width-sensitive part.

title: mHC: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections
one_line: Projects hyper-connection mixing matrices onto doubly stochastic matrices for stability and reports gains over HC.
formula: mixing matrix projected onto the Birkhoff polytope with Sinkhorn-Knopp

title: Towards a Principled Muon under muP: Ensuring Spectral Conditions throughout Training
one_line: Proposes a modified Muon that keeps muP spectral conditions during training so the learning rate transfers across widths without explicit weight normalization.

title: Conditional Memory via Scalable Lookup: A New Axis of Sparsity for Large Language Models
one_line: Engram adds an N-gram embedding lookup table as a sparse memory next to MoE layers.

title: Universal Dynamics of Warmup Stable Decay: understanding WSD beyond Transformers
one_line: Compares WSD training signals in a small language model and a small CNN; decay share is not varied.

title: Curriculum Learning for LLM Pretraining: An Analysis of Learning Dynamics
one_line: From 14M to 410M parameters, curriculum gains are mostly in stability and mostly in smaller models.

title: IMU-1: Sample-Efficient Pre-training of Small Language Models
one_line: A recipe for sample-efficient small-model pretraining with component ablations, including the schedule.

title: Delving into Muon and Beyond: Deep Analysis and Extensions
one_line: Treats Muon as spectral normalization and finds it does not always beat Adam-type optimizers.

title: Optimal Learning-Rate Schedules under Functional Scaling Laws: Power Decay and Warmup-Stable-Decay
one_line: Derives which LR schedule minimizes final loss under a functional scaling law, and identifies power decay and warmup-stable-decay as the resulting shapes.

title: Convex Dominance in Deep Learning I
one_line: Proposes one law that predicts both the loss and the optimal learning rate from a single fit (search snippet only; body not read).

title: Weight Decay Improves Language Model Plasticity
one_line: Reports that heavier weight decay in pretraining makes the base model adapt better after fine-tuning and reduces overfitting, though it does not measure forgetting of pretraining facts.

title: Extending muP: Spectral Conditions for Feature Learning Across Optimizers
one_line: Derives muP-type spectral scaling conditions for several optimizers including Muon and reports zero-shot learning-rate transfer across widths.

title: Pre-training LLM without Learning Rate Decay Enhances Supervised Fine-Tuning
one_line: A constant learning rate after warmup gives better fine-tuning results than decayed schedules.

title: Muown: Row-Norm Control for Muon Optimization
one_line: Muon without weight decay drifts in spectral norm, mainly through row magnitudes; a row-norm variable controls it.

title: Quantifying Hyperparameter Transfer and the Importance of Embedding Layer Learning Rate
one_line: Measures how well hyperparameters transfer across width and finds the embedding learning rate matters most.

title: Gated DeltaNet-2: Decoupling Erase and Write in Linear Attention
one_line: At 1.3B parameters and 100B tokens, Gated DeltaNet-2 beats Mamba2 and Kimi Delta Attention, most on retrieval.

title: Forgetting in Language Models: Capacity, Optimization, and Self-Generated Replay
one_line: Lower learning rates reduce forgetting but need many more steps where capacity is not limiting; replay of self-generated samples nearly removes forgetting, so high-learning-rate finetuning becomes viable.

title: Spectral Scaling Laws of Muon
one_line: Measures the spectrum of Muon's momentum buffer across layers and sizes and picks Newton-Schulz steps per layer.

title: Linear Attention Architectures: Mechanisms, Trade-offs, and Cross-Layer Routing
one_line: Runs matched 350M-parameter, 15B-token training of softmax attention against DeltaNet and Gated DeltaNet variants; the fetched text gives throughput and learning-rate notes but no softmax-vs-Gated-DeltaNet validation-loss numbers.

title: Regularize or Localize: When Training-Time KV-Cache Geometry Pays Under Quantization
one_line: An anti-collapse term during language-model training helps KV-cache geometry only under coarse quantization.

title: Scale Weight Decay and Train Better
one_line: Tracks the RMS weight norm of a matrix under Muon with decoupled decay, comparing constant and scaled decay.
